summary: Configured node1 as an internal DNS resolver using dnsmasq, resolving inventory-api.internal to node2's IP (10.100.174.11) and forwarding all other queries upstream. Configured node2's NetworkManager eth0 connection profile to use node1 (10.100.174.10) as its DNS resolver, persisted via ipv4.dns/ipv4.ignore-auto-dns. Verified resolution end-to-end from node2, then restarted each node one at a time, confirmed a changed boot ID as proof of actual restart, and verified full recovery of dnsmasq and DNS resolution on both nodes afterward.
actions_performed: Diagnosed RHEL7 nodes with no enabled subscription-manager repos; used vault.centos.org as a temporary EL7-compatible repo to install dnsmasq (node1) and bind-utils (both nodes) for testing, then removed the temp repo file

Installed and configured dnsmasq on node1 via /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf: address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.174.11, no-resolv, upstream server=10.100.174.1, listen-address=127.0.0.1,10.100.174.10, bind-interfaces
Enabled and started dnsmasq on node1; opened firewalld 'dns' service permanently
Verified dnsmasq resolves inventory-api.internal to node2 and forwards other queries upstream correctly
Configured node2's NetworkManager eth0 connection with ipv4.dns=10.100.174.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes via nmcli, reapplied the connection; verified /etc/resolv.conf updated and resolution works
Captured baseline boot_id and service health on both nodes
Restarted node1 via 'sudo shutdown -r now', polled until SSH returned, confirmed new boot_id and full dnsmasq/firewall/resolution recovery, then verified node2 resolution was unaffected

Restarted node2 via 'sudo shutdown -r now', polled until SSH returned, confirmed new boot_id, and verified resolv.conf, NM profile persistence, and inventory-api.internal resolution all recovered correctly

evidence.requirement: node1 runs internal DNS resolver mapping inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed, configured with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.174.11, started/enabled, and dig confirms resolution to node2's IP plus upstream passthrough for other names

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: nmcli set ipv4.dns=10.100.174.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes on node2's eth0 connection; resolv.conf shows nameserver 10.100.174.10; dig/getent resolve inventory-api.internal to 10.100.174.11; upstream lookups (www.redhat.com) still work via forwarding
Captured boot_id 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799 and confirmed dnsmasq active/enabled with successful local resolution

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged (connection closed by remote host), polling later returned new boot_id 25c1af7f-2bed-4b99-9ddb-f29658eea331, proving an actual restart occurred
dnsmasq active and enabled post-restart, firewalld dns service persisted, dig confirms inventory-api.internal still resolves to node2, and node2's independent lookup against node1 also succeeds
Captured boot_id d72bd4ec-4e55-42df-9c71-99b4f4ace0ec and confirmed resolv.conf pointed at node1 with working resolution

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged (connection closed by remote host), polling later returned new boot_id 6cb40733-4446-413f-9222-78626d38c456, proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart resolv.conf still shows nameserver 10.100.174.10, NM connection profile retains ipv4.dns/ipv4.ignore-auto-dns settings, and dig/getent confirm inventory-api.internal resolves to 10.100.174.11
